notes: Zone scatter for procedural street detail. Coordinates are world metres: +X east, +Z south (the game's frame).
Zone shapes and scatter densities are production inference for the ferry-arrival pilot, not survey data.
Step 0 scatter emits placement slots only; later steps assign assets per slot kind. The runtime builds nothing from slots yet.

Exclusions are the shared mask for every street-detail source. The older vegetation clearances (roads 4 m, buildings 5 m, spawn 24 m, ferry path 16 m, QA route 7 m) size tree canopies; these values size walk, camera and doorway clearance instead.

Always-on street ground for the pilot zones: kerbs and raised sidewalks, curb ramps, road paint and asphalt wear, built by tools/lib/street-ground-generation.mjs into the chunk records. A zone without a ground block gets none.

Dimensions are production inference read from the dated pilot photos (Sep 2025 Treasure Island Road, ferry plaza and Building 1 forecourt; Sep and Nov 2025 Avenue of the Palms), not survey data. Road ribbons keep the frozen generator widths; parking lanes add asphalt beside them.

Collision: sidewalk tops are solid at the road surface plus reveal_m. The stock player has no step-up (floor_snap_length 0.35 m, floor_max_angle 48 degrees), so every curb face has an invisible collision ramp support_run_m wide in front of it, back edges a visible slope back_slope_run_m wide and curb-ramp sides a flare flare_run_m wide; the generator rejects any of them steeper than 40 degrees.
Wear densities are decals per 100 m2 of asphalt in the zone: low in the new district, more on older roads and the forecourt lot.

Sidewalks are poured concrete in panel_m squares that follow the street. closing_m fills gaps narrower than twice it between raised pieces. A zone with planting curb_strip turns the raised ground between the curb and a sidewalk set back by planting_gap_m or more, and the ground beyond the default sidewalk where an OSM sidewalk crowds the curb, into mulch beds (Avenue of the Palms, Sep 2025 photos ih02 and ih05). planting_behind_walk names OSM sidewalks photographed at the curb instead: the default walk stays there and the bed takes the ground behind it.
A plaza is a concrete walk walk_m wide at the curb plus banded paving out to depth_m, on the side of its roads nearest side_point_xz, clipped to its zone.

parking_lanes add width_m of asphalt beyond the frozen ribbon on both sides of the listed roads inside the zone; the curb, its ramps and the sidewalk move out with it (Avenue of the Palms: cars park along both curbs in Sep 2025 ih02 and ih05).
centerlines picks a style per road class: double_yellow, or dashed_faded (a worn yellow dash dash_m long every dash_m + dash_gap_m).
